correctness.rationale: Exact two-by-two inverse yields the precision identity. Parametrizing the reciprocal-cost constraint by a unit-interval coordinate reduces the entire feasible family to one variable. The global exponential inequality controls all endpoint-dependent sequences. The unique maximizer of the resulting cubic gives the sharp coefficient \(12\sqrt3/\ell\); a fixed-ratio construction attains it and compactness proves the unique asymptotic ratio. The analytical argument is supplemented by 114 symbolic/numerical consistency checks.

value.rationale: For exactly the first-order inverse-cost setup considered in GRE experimental design, the new result resolves the continuously optimized rough-kernel two-fidelity regime, provides an exact universal fidelity ratio and constant, and proves a one-power budget advantage over a single simulation. This clarifies the limitation of heuristic conclusions from a fixed grid. Restricted fixed-scale posterior variance is a substantive, motivated design invariant.
